headline: 36 contract addresses catalogued across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and BNB Chain.

findings.text: Block-explorer search surfaced Railgun-tagged Ethereum, Polygon, and BNB Chain addresses; Arbitrum explorer search did not surface a reliable Railgun tag in this run.
Official docs point developers to the Railgun deployments repository for deployment addresses.
The ABDK and Hacken audit PDFs were fetched; Hacken lists audited contract files at commit d2c63577ddd8310c87dced0d549cf9505b372111, while the pinned Zokyo URL failed to fetch.
The Railgun deployments repository exposes per-chain TypeScript deployment configs for Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and BNB Chain.
All four pinned chains were enumerated from the deployments repository; each chain has separate address entries.
No factory address or child-enumeration view was identified from the fetched deployment configs.
Catalogued addresses use the required role taxonomy with actor_class set to unknown except where an explorer tag indicates a contract label only, not signer composition.
Every address in admin_addresses traces to a fetched docs, GitHub deployment, token-doc, or explorer URL.

rationale.verdict: Discovery-only slice: walked official docs, deployment configs, audits, and explorer/search surfaces; catalogued 36 addresses, with unresolved audit URL and Arbitrum explorer-tag gaps.

evidence.shows: Capability probe succeeded against the protocol website; page title identifies RAILGUN as an on-chain ZK privacy ecosystem.

Official developer guide links to the contracts repo and deployments repo, states deployment addresses can be viewed in the deployments repo, and describes the main proxy as an EIP1967 Transparent Upgradeable Proxy.
Official deployments repository README says it contains deployment configs and artifacts for each chain.
Official contracts repository for Railgun smart contracts.
Railgun Engine SDK repository describes itself as a JavaScript library to interact with Railgun smart contracts and private balances.

Railgun docs describe RAILGUN as an on-chain privacy system for Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, and Arbitrum using ZK cryptography; docs also state users get confidential 0zk addresses, the protocol is non-custodial, and code is publicly viewable.
Docs state Railgun enables private interaction with native smart contracts and DeFi through ZK proofs and Adapt Modules.
Docs list RAIL token addresses for Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, and Polygon and describe RAIL as the protocol security token.
Docs list the BNB Smart Chain RAILBSC token address.
Docs list the Polygon RAILPOLY token address.
Etherscan labels this Ethereum address as Railgun: RAIL Token.
Etherscan labels this Ethereum address as Railgun: Relay.
Etherscan labels this Ethereum address as Railgun: Treasury.
Etherscan labels this Ethereum address as RAILGUN: Staking and indicates it may be a proxy contract.
PolygonScan search surfaced a Railgun-related deployer-labelled address.
BscScan search surfaced a BNB Chain address labelled Railgun: Relay.
Ethereum deployment config lists delegator, getters, governor rewards, implementation, proxy, proxyAdmin, RAIL token, staking, treasury, and voting addresses.
Polygon deployment config lists delegator, getters, governor rewards, implementation, proxy, proxyAdmin, RAILPOLY token, staking, treasury, and voting addresses.
Arbitrum deployment config lists delegator, implementation, L1Sender, L2Executor, proxy, proxyAdmin, treasury implementation, and treasury proxy addresses.
BNB Chain deployment config lists delegator, getters, governor rewards, implementation, proxy, proxyAdmin, RAILBSC token, staking, treasury, and voting addresses.
ABDK audit report for Railgun smart contracts and circuits, dated 2 July 2021, states it evaluated sending, receiving, and smart-contract interaction privacy functionality.

Hacken audit report lists repository https://github.com/Railgun-Privacy/contract, commit d2c63577ddd8310c87dced0d549cf9505b372111, and in-scope contracts including governance, logic, proxy, token, and treasury contracts.

unknowns: D1: Arbitrum explorer name-tag search did not return a reliable Railgun-tagged address in this run; Arbitrum addresses are sourced from the official deployments repository instead.
D2: No standalone docs page titled deployed contracts or addresses was found beyond the official docs pointing to the deployments repository.

D3: Pinned Zokyo November 2021 audit URL failed with a 404 after redirect from assets.railgun.ch to assets.railgun.org; search surfaced later Zokyo PDFs but they were not fully opened successfully in this run.
D4: GitHub deployment files were fetched on master, but the fetch surface did not expose a usable current commit SHA for content-addressed deployment citations.
D5: Explorer name-tag coverage was incomplete on Arbitrum despite deployment repository coverage.
D6: No factory address with allPools/getPool/getMarket/getVault-style enumeration was identified from fetched materials.
D7: Actor classes for proxyAdmin, treasury, voting, relay, and staking contracts were not bytecode-read or Safe-owner-read in this discovery run.
D8: Addresses from explorer snippet-only search results that lacked official deployment corroboration were not included unless they appeared in fetched deployment/docs pages.

protocol_metadata.about: RAILGUN is an on-chain privacy system for Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, and Arbitrum. Users can move tokens into Railgun smart contracts, receive confidential 0zk addresses, and transfer, swap, lend, borrow, or call dApps privately without leaving the underlying chain. Developers integrate the system through SDKs and Adapt Modules that let existing dApps add private smart-contract interactions.
